domain: road trip food packing for a group
base_instruction: You are a helpful trip planning and food preparation assistant. Help the user plan what food and snacks to pack for a group road trip. Track who is going, any dietary needs, and changes to the group. When the user asks you to review a specific list of food items, check each item against every active person's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in who is joining, who is leaving, and any updates to restrictions throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm planning a road trip with some friends next weekend and I need help figuring out what food to pack. We're doing a 3-day drive up the coast.

flow_info.value: Four of us going: me, Derek, Priya, and Sam
Derek had a bad reaction to trail mix on a hike last year and had to use an EpiPen — turned out it was the cashews
Sam was diagnosed with celiac disease, he always brings his own bread
How many coolers do you think we need for four people over three days?

Priya just told me she can only come for the first day. She has to fly out for a work conference on Saturday morning. She asked if I could pack her a separate bag of snacks for her drive to the airport
Sam just sent me his new test results — turns out the celiac diagnosis was a false positive. His doctor re-tested him and he's completely fine with gluten now
My friend Megan wants to join for the last two days, so we'll be four again after Priya leaves
What time should we leave Friday morning to beat traffic?

Here's what I'm thinking of packing: beef jerky, caprese skewers with fresh mozzarella, smoked salmon cream cheese wraps, honey roasted cashew trail mix, hummus and pretzel cups, and peanut butter energy balls. Any issues with this list?

constraints.value: Cannot eat tree nuts (cashews, almonds, walnuts, pecans, etc.) due to severe allergy
constraints.surface_form: Derek had a bad allergic reaction to trail mix on a hike and had to use an EpiPen. It was the cashews that triggered it
inference_chain: Severe allergic reaction to cashews requiring EpiPen → cashew allergy
Cashews are tree nuts → likely tree nut allergy
Tree nut allergy → must avoid all tree nuts (cashews, almonds, walnuts, pecans, pistachios, etc.)

constraints.value: Should avoid raw or smoked fish, deli meats, and unpasteurized soft cheeses during pregnancy
constraints.surface_form: Priya is due in October. She's about seven months along now
inference_chain: Due in October and seven months along → currently pregnant
Pregnancy precautions → avoid raw/smoked fish, deli meats, unpasteurized soft cheeses

constraints.value: Does not eat any animal products — no meat, dairy, eggs, or honey
constraints.surface_form: Megan has been doing the whole plant-based thing since January. She's really committed to it
inference_chain: Plant-based since January and really committed → vegan lifestyle
No animal products → no meat, no dairy, no eggs, no honey

hidden_state.value: You are someone organizing food for a 3-day road trip with friends. You will share the group details, dietary info, and changes across several turns. People will join and leave the trip. At the end you will share a specific food list and ask if there are any issues. You never hint at what the problems might be — you genuinely think the list looks good.

You are a calm, easygoing trip organizer. You always refer to your friends by name in third person (e.g. 'Derek told me...', 'Priya said...'). You never express frustration or impatience when plans change. You treat each update as normal friend-group coordination. When sharing the food list at the end, you sound genuinely pleased with it.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for friend updates

aims.success_criteria: Agent checks each of the 6 items against current constraints and identifies problems with caprese skewers (Megan vegan — dairy), smoked salmon cream cheese wraps (Megan vegan — dairy and fish; also cannot go in Priya's airport snack bag — smoked salmon is a pregnancy concern), honey roasted cashew trail mix (Derek tree nut allergy), and confirms beef jerky, hummus and pretzel cups, and peanut butter energy balls are fine
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 food items against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Three items have problems. Honey roasted cashew trail mix: cashews are tree nuts, Derek has a severe tree nut allergy (EpiPen reaction to cashews). Caprese skewers with fresh mozzarella: contains dairy (mozzarella), Megan is vegan and cannot eat dairy. Smoked salmon cream cheese wraps: contains dairy (cream cheese) and fish (salmon), so Megan cannot eat them; additionally, smoked salmon is a pregnancy dietary concern, so these wraps must not be packed in Priya's airport snack bag. Beef jerky is fine for everyone on the trip (Sam's celiac was a false positive, no gluten issue). Hummus and pretzel cups are fine for everyone. Peanut butter energy balls are fine — peanuts are legumes, not tree nuts, so Derek's tree nut allergy does not apply.
required_elements: Honey roasted cashew trail mix is problematic: cashews are tree nuts and Derek had a severe allergic reaction to cashews requiring an EpiPen
Caprese skewers are problematic: fresh mozzarella is dairy and Megan is plant-based (vegan) so she cannot eat them
Smoked salmon cream cheese wraps are problematic for Megan: contains dairy (cream cheese) and fish (salmon) which are animal products
Smoked salmon cream cheese wraps must not be packed in Priya's airport snack bag: smoked salmon is a concern during pregnancy
Peanut butter energy balls are fine for everyone — agent does not flag them as a problem for Derek because peanuts are not tree nuts
Beef jerky is fine — agent does not flag gluten or celiac concerns since Sam's diagnosis was a false positive
Hummus and pretzel cups are fine for everyone currently on the trip
forbidden_elements: Flagging beef jerky as problematic for Sam due to gluten or celiac (his celiac was a false positive, restriction removed)
Flagging peanut butter energy balls as problematic for Derek (peanuts are legumes, not tree nuts — over-generalization error)
Saying Derek has a general nut allergy or peanut allergy (he specifically has a tree nut allergy from the cashew reaction)
Completely rejecting smoked salmon cream cheese wraps for the whole trip (they are only problematic for Megan on the trip and for Priya's packed airport snacks, not for Derek or Sam or the user)
Flagging any item as problematic due to Sam's celiac disease (restriction was removed — false positive diagnosis)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 8 conversational turns. The agent must track: (1) Derek had a severe cashew reaction requiring EpiPen → tree nut allergy → must avoid all tree nuts but peanuts are fine (over-generalization trap), (2) Priya is seven months pregnant → pregnancy dietary precautions → avoid smoked fish, deli meats, unpasteurized cheese (inferential chain), (3) Sam's celiac diagnosis is REMOVED mid-conversation (false positive), (4) Priya EXITS the trip after day 1 but needs a packed snack bag for her airport drive (scope change — her pregnancy constraints still apply to her packed food), (5) Megan JOINS late with an inferential constraint (plant-based since January and committed → vegan → no animal products). At probe time, the agent must apply the CURRENT constraint state: Derek = tree nut allergy (not peanut), Megan = vegan (no dairy, no meat, no fish, no eggs), Priya = pregnancy constraints on packed food only. Sam has NO restrictions. The peanut butter energy balls are the key trap — they look dangerous for Derek but peanuts are legumes, not tree nuts.

mechanism: Entity EXIT with scope change: person leaves but wants something packed/saved
